title: "V5001 impure_contract"
description: "Predicates in where, requires, ensures and property bodies must be pure, terminating and deterministic: no loops, no recursion, and calls only to @total functions in the contract subset (design §7.1)."
---

An error from the `contract` phase. `sakura explain V5001` prints this explanation offline.

Predicates in `where`, `requires`, `ensures` and `property` bodies must be pure, terminating and
deterministic: no loops, no recursion, and calls only to `@total` functions in the contract
subset (design §7.1). Move effects out of the predicate and mark the helper it calls `@total`.

Wrong:

```sakura
fn noisy_positive(x: Int) -> Bool ! {Console} { Console.print("checking"); x > 0 }
fn halve(x: Int) -> Int ! {Console} requires noisy_positive(x) { x / 2 }
```

Fixed:

```sakura
@total
fn positive(x: Int) -> Bool { x > 0 }
fn halve(x: Int) -> Int requires positive(x) { x / 2 }
```

## Wrong program

[`compiler/tests/ui/V5001_impure_contract.sakura`](https://github.com/icantcodefyi/sakuralang/blob/master/compiler/tests/ui/V5001_impure_contract.sakura), which the compiler's ui suite runs through `sakura check`:

```sakura
fn noisy_positive(x: Int) -> Bool ! {Console} {
  Console.print("checking")
  x > 0
}

fn halve(x: Int) -> Int
  ! {Console}
  requires noisy_positive(x)
{ x / 2 }
```

## Fixed program

[`compiler/tests/ui/V5001_impure_contract.fixed.sakura`](https://github.com/icantcodefyi/sakuralang/blob/master/compiler/tests/ui/V5001_impure_contract.fixed.sakura), which `sakura check` accepts with no diagnostics:

```sakura
@total
fn positive(x: Int) -> Bool { x > 0 }

fn halve(x: Int) -> Int
  requires positive(x)
{ x / 2 }
```
